title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Effects on the Environment and on Organisms
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 8, Extension Topic B · 9 questions · 90 marks · 31 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question, and nothing here is constructed. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question.

Do Cluster 1 first. LO (b)'s own wording is effects of climate change as a result of greenhouse gas emissions, so without the absorb-and-re-emit chain from Cluster 1 there is no cause to attach any of this to.

Mangroves and sequestration lead this drill. The specimen spent a whole Paper 1 stem on it and an 11-mark Paper 3 question on the same node, so Question 1 is that specimen stem, all four options audited.

Question 2 is the full-cycle question, 11 marks, and it runs the whole coral chain: the symbiosis both ways, the bleaching sequence in order, then ocean acidification from dissolved carbon dioxide through carbonic acid, hydrogen ions and carbonate ions to a skeleton that stops forming and starts dissolving. Your notes get that chain wrong. They say corals cannot absorb the calcium carbonate they need. Corals do not absorb calcium carbonate, they deposit it. Learn the mark scheme's version.

Five real figures, six questions figure-led. Book 8 is 52.6% figure-led and 49.7% data interpretation, both the highest of any Book, and this cluster's two concept headings are the two most figure-led blocks in the whole Biology the papers at 52% and 61%. Two figures could not be recovered from the source papers and carry the paper's own description instead, which is said in the Sources block of the question concerned. No part asks you to state a value at a year: the data is stimulus for a describe-with-data, an explain, a suggest or an evaluate.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then makes you justify every option.

Cumulative over Books 1, 5 and 7. Q6(c) needs enzyme denaturation and stomatal closure said cold. Q8(a) needs the Q10 rule and the shape of the enzyme-temperature curve. Q8(c) needs directional selection applied to a melanic polymorphism. A Book 1, 5 or 7 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Book 8 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. When a stem says with reference to or using the figure, quote a value, its unit and its interval, then account for it; a scheme in this set states that each point must include duration, coral coverage % and temperature in °C, and that no mark is awarded for any point read off the wrong graph or axis. Say that the zooxanthellae are expelled while still alive, because the opposite is a recorded misconception. Never let corals migrate; a scheme rejects that by name because corals are sessile. On feedback, classify the loop that is printed on the paper, do not recite the one you memorised. On insects, state a direction of change, because an examiner comment treats affect as vague.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 why mangrove sediment stores carbon, and mitigation held apart from adaptation · Q2 the coral chain end to end, symbiosis to bleaching to a dissolving skeleton · Q3 classifying a feedback network that is printed on the paper · Q4 LO (b)'s physical effects as short causal chains attached to real data · Q5 what a data quote has to contain, at the granularity the scheme states · Q6 range shift read off a new figure, and the limits of the inference · Q7 two species shifting in opposite directions and the mismatch that follows · Q8 the insect temperature curve, up and then down · Q9 the LO (b) sweep at full essay length.

The two deliberately shared marking points, declared. First, heat stress makes coral polyps expel their zooxanthellae, so the coral loses its photosynthetic food supply and starves, which Q2(b) and Q2(c) need as mechanism and Q9 needs as one of thirteen possible marks in a category that requires two; the three are marked on different things, the sequence, the proximate trigger, and breadth across categories. Second, increased temperature raises insect metabolic rate and shortens the life cycle, which Q7(b) needs for caterpillars and Q8(b) needs as one of five impacts; Q7(b) is marked on tying it to a dated phenological shift and Q8(b) on breadth with a direction of change attached to each. Every other required answer in the set is unique.

Nothing from Book 9, and nothing from Cluster 1 or Cluster 3. The carbon cycle, carbon footprints and the greenhouse mechanism itself are Cluster 1 and are assumed here rather than retested. Food security, biodiversity of the tropics, the Aedes aegypti life cycle and the spread of dengue beyond the tropics are Cluster 3. Dengue virology, serotypes and the host immune response are Extension Topic A and are out of scope for Book 8 entirely.
